sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Massively Multiplayer Online Role-Playing Games

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law), as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended; Law of 24 March 1989 on the Luxembourg business register (RCS); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 18 February 2019 on the operational implementation of the RBE.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of constitutional documents of each direct shareholder/partner (e.g., articles of association, partnership agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce / competent authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or extract from the foreign business registry for each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry or competent registrar

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and proof of residential address for each individual UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local notary or authorized public officer in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-wealth declaration for each UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution or licensed auditor in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae / professional background summary for each individual UBO and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The individual UBO or general partner

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Luxembourg's national AML/CFT framework, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and Interpol/domestic PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any UBO or partner who is a politically exposed person (PEP) or who has family/close associates qualifying as PEPs. Screening must be completed prior to incorporation and refreshed at minimum annually during the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Luxembourg Business Register), accessible via the e-RCS portal at https://www.lbr.lu and the official RCS online query system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp name may be submitted in any language using Latin characters, but the statutory name must be preceded or followed by the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the acronym 'SCSp'. Luxembourg has no mandatory local alphabet transliteration requirement; however, all official documentary filings with the RCS and notarial acts must be in French, German, or Luxembourgish, and any non-Latin script name must be transliterated into a Latin-alphabet version.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name, the applicant must submit a formal written appeal to the RCS Registration Department within 15 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the rejected name, a revised name alternative, and any supporting legal arguments or trademark/trade-name evidence. If the rejection is based on a misleading or prohibited token, the applicant may submit regulatory authorization from the competent ministry or a substantiated justification that the activity is genuinely licensed. The RCS must issue a decision within 10 business days; if the appeal is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the administrative tribunal of Luxembourg within three months of the negative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered address service is permissible for the SCSp provided that a Luxembourg-based independent service provider (e.g., a law firm, service company, or fiduciary) maintains an official registered address in Luxembourg and receives all official correspondence. The virtual office must not be used to misrepresent the actual operational substance; however, for a pure holding or investment partnership (including MMORPG publishing royalty/asset holding) no physical local operational staff is required at pre-incorporation stage. The registered address must be a physical address in Luxembourg, and the service provider must be licensed under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 to provide fiduciary or corporate services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: quantified risk of 5% for an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first 12 months after incorporation, given that the SCSp is a tax-transparent partnership with no employees, no physical inventory, and no licensable banking or financial activity. The risk may rise to 15% if the entity holds significant digital/intangible assets or if the RBE/UBO documentation raises inconsistencies. The RCS and the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) may perform off-site document inspections with a higher probability (20%) based on automated AML/CFT risk scoring.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard SCSp notarial deed without complex partner provisions (€1,200–€1,800)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary statutory registration fee to the RCS for official incorporation (dépôt au RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RCS filing fee (€75) plus surcharge (€20) converted at EUR/USD 1.20

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence on UBOs, OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, and PEP background checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Luxembourg corporate counsel / AML compliance provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for hourly legal work (6–8 hours at €180–€220/hour)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization costs for foreign public documents and notarized copies (estimated for 5 documents from up to 3 foreign jurisdictions)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities (e.g., US Secretary of State / US Department of State; Singapore Academy of Law; Hong Kong High Court)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Average $25–$100 per document including translation/certification if required

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation of foreign documents into French/German/English (if required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of €0.15–€0.30 per word; estimated 500–800 words per bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service / virtual office arrangement (first-year fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of €800–€1,200 per year for a registered address without accounting/administrative services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration fee with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RBE filing fee (€60) converted at EUR/USD 1.20

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 137-1 et seq. (société en commandite spéciale), introduced by Law of 11 July 2013
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement / Deed of Constitution (acte de constitution), filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required by law for an SCSp. Contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement. There is no mandatory escrow account; the SCSp must have at least one general partner with unlimited liability and one limited partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned sole general partner of the SCSp, acting as its ultimate governing body, unanimously resolves: (i) to approve the subscription of partnership interests by the general partner and limited partners as specified in Schedules A and B; (ii) to adopt as the registered office the address 15 Boulevard du Jazz, L-4370 Belvaux, Luxembourg; (iii) to appoint [Name] as gérant-manager, authorised to represent the partnership, open bank accounts, and execute all contracts; (iv) to ratify the filing of the constitution deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers and publication in the RESA; (v) to authorise the manager to make all tax, VAT, and employment registrations and to execute any ancillary documents necessary to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Vetting and Drafting of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS Online Portal (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search through the LBR online business register portal. Engage a Luxembourg notary or eligible lawyer to draft the private deed of constitution and the limited partnership agreement in accordance with Articles 137-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915. The deed must identify the general partner, limited partners, contribution amounts, profit-sharing rules, and management powers. Notarization is mandatory only if any contribution is made by real property or where a public offering of partnership interests is intended; otherwise a private deed signed by all partners is sufficient.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement / deed of constitution
Passports or national identity cards of all partners
General partner's directors' identification documents
Name availability printout from LBR
Power of attorney for the incorporator, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is rejected or the deed is returned for correction, amend the instrument and refile promptly through the same portal. LBR may require clarification of the legal form or reserved name; submit a corrective deed or explanatory memorandum within 15 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The gérant-manager opens a bank account in the name of the SCSp and arranges for the initial capital contributions to be wired by each partner in accordance with the partnership agreement. Although no statutory minimum capital exists, a deposit confirmation (attestation d'ouverture de compte) is typically required by the RCS and by service providers for AML/KYC compliance. If contributions are made in kind, obtain an independent valuation report and attach it to the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Identification documents of the general partner and ultimate beneficial owners
Bank account opening forms and deposit instructions
Proof of origin of funds and economic rationale
Capital contribution confirmation or valuation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC information, provide source-of-wealth documentation and a simple business plan. If the account is denied, choose another Luxembourg or EU credit institution and restart the KYC process, ensuring that the account opening certificate is reissued in the exact SCSp legal name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarised or private deed, together with the account certificate and all mandatory annexes, through the LBR e-filing platform. The application must specify the SCSp's registered office address, name, form, duration if limited, and the identity of the general partner. Upon validation, the RCS issues an extract, a business identification number (matricule) and a certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement / deed of constitution
Copy of bank account opening certificate
Registered office lease or proof of right to occupy the address
Consent of the gérant-manager to act
Declaration of non-disqualification of the general partner
Completed Form A/incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or a refusal, correct the deficiencies and resubmit the application within the stated deadline. Legal counsel can file observations and request an administrative rectification; upon final rejection, appeal to the Luxembourg District Court within the statutory time limit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, obtain the official registration extract and submit the mandatory publication data to the RESA through the LBR online interface. The published extract covers the legal form, name, registered office, object, general partner's identity, and managers. This publication protects third parties and triggers the commencement of legal effects against the public.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Proof of payment of publication fees
Text of the deed provisions concerning the legal form, name, registered office, and object
Identity of registered managers/générant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is inaccurate or delayed, request a correction note through the LBR portal. Any discrepancy with the RCS data must be reconciled by filing an amending deed and obtaining a fresh RCS extract before the corrected RESA entry is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp with the AEDT for VAT obligations and income/corporate tax filing purposes, even though the SCSp is fiscally transparent. Obtain a Luxembourg VAT number if taxable supplies cross the applicable threshold. Register with the CCSS for social security if any employees are hired. The tax registration confirms the partnership's matricule and links it to the national tax database for withholding and annual filing requirements.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and certificate of incorporation
Limited partnership agreement
Identification of the general partner and manager
Proof of registered office address
Estimated turnover and VAT status declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT rejects the registration or asks for supplementary data, provide a translation of the partnership agreement into French/German and a clear organizational chart of the partners. Use the AEDT online portal to track the case; unresolved issues may be escalated to the Renewal and Registration Service of the AEDT.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale de l'Industrie et des Technologies (no industrial license required for software publishing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for ISIC 5820 publishing of software; the main legal prerequisites are the RCS registration and the applicable consumer and GDPR data-protection filings.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal EIA for office-based software publishing operations; no installation classed under the Luxembourg classification of classified installations (Commensurabilité) if activities are restricted to administrative and digital services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply. Compliance obligations are limited to the general Environmental Law of 31 May 1999 regarding waste separation, WEEE collection under the Offices and Electronics Directive, and energy certificates for premises. Office waste must be sorted according to municipal rules and data-storage hardware must be disposed via authorised e-waste channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours) is required for the registered office if open to employees or the public; structural load and electrical safety inspections must satisfy the communal service for construction permits (service de l'urbanisme). The Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) must approve workplace ergonomics, emergency exits, and ensure compliance with the Labour Code (Code du travail) for IT staff working at screens.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) for income, corporate and withholding tax — www.impotsdirects.lu; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT / Luxembourg VAT Authority) for VAT registration and VAT compliance — aedt.public.lu; integrated digital filings are submitted through MyGuichet.lu at guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or operating through an SCSp must first register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR) to obtain a national business identification number if the SCSp is filed with the RCS. For VAT, the non-established taxable person must file Form 640 'Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA' with the AEDT, attaching proof of foreign business registration, identity documents for the general partner/managers, and a power of attorney or tax representation mandate. Non-EU persons without an EU establishment must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative before a LU VAT number is issued. The LU VAT identification number has the format LU followed by 8 digits. For Luxembourg income tax, the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default; each partner is separately liable and, to the extent taxable in Luxembourg, must obtain or use a Luxembourg national identification number. If the Article 168bis LIR opacity election is made, the SCSp obtains its own CIT/NWT identification number from the ACD upon filing the election and registration in the RCS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Under Article 168bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR), a fiscally transparent partnership such as the SCSp may file an irrevocable opacity election to be treated as a Luxembourg corporate taxpayer subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; otherwise, the SCSp is fiscally transparent and its profits are taxed at partner level. Partnership-level municipal business tax may nevertheless arise if the SCSp carries on a commercial activity. Anti-hybrid rules implementing ATAD (notably in Article 168sexies LIR) restrict hybrid mismatch outcomes and may re-characterise the SCSp where counterparties treat it inconsistently. For VAT, separate election forms apply for VAT grouping as a single taxable person (assujetti unique) and for the EU OSS scheme.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC; standard rate 17%, reduced rates 14%, 8% and 3%; digital services supplied by a Luxembourg-established SCSp to EU consumers are generally taxed at the rate applicable in the consumer's EU member state pursuant to the destination principle
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 25,000 annual taxable turnover for domestically established small enterprises under the Luxembourg small-business exemption; no de minimis threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of electronically supplied services or to intra-EU acquisitions, so foreign entities making taxable supplies of MMORPG digital services in Luxembourg/EU must register or use the OSS from the first euro
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls or digital stamping regime. Electronic invoicing is permitted in B2B transactions provided the authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility are assured, e.g. via EDI or PEPPOL. E-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers to Luxembourg public-sector entities in the format required by European standard EN 16931/PEPPOL. VAT returns must be filed electronically via the eCDF module on MyGuichet.lu; monthly or quarterly returns are due by the twentieth day of the following month or quarter, with annual recapitulative statements where applicable. OSS filings follow the standard monthly calendar of the member state of identification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available where goods are physically exported from the EU to a non-EU destination and where cross-border services fall outside the Luxembourg place-of-supply rules. For MMORPG digital services: (i) B2B supplies to a business customer established outside the EU are zero-rated or outside Luxembourg VAT scope; (ii) B2C electronic supplies to non-EU consumers are outside the EU VAT scope and may be reported as export services; (iii) B2C digital supplies to EU consumers cannot be zero-rated and must be declared via the Union OSS at the consumer's member state rate. The taxpayer must demonstrably establish the customer's business/residential location, the actual performance of the service, and receipt of payment from outside Luxembourg/EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Proof of physical exit from the EU (customs exit verification, forwarder certificate or equivalent)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow zero-rating if the export or service export is not substantiated within the statutory records period, assessing undeclared VAT at the 17% standard rate, plus default interest of 0.6% per month and administrative fines ranging from 10% to 50% of the tax due, rising up to 100% in cases of deliberate concealment. Fraudulent documentation may also trigger criminal tax evasion penalties under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, joint liability of partners/managers, and mandatory AML reporting of forged invoicing. The ordinary VAT assessment limitation period is five years, extended to ten years for fraud, enabling long-period retrospective clawbacks and reclassification of zero-rated flows.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as national central bank integrated in the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and payment institutions; there is no separate foreign exchange administration in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full and unrestricted currency convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. No exchange control authorisation, currency licence, tax clearances, or prior approval is required for remittance of profits, distribution of proceeds, or repatriation of investor capital. The introduction of capital into or withdrawal of capital from the SCSp is subject only to ordinary anti-money-laundering verification by the receiving bank, EU/UN sanctions screening, and optional balance-of-payments statistical reporting by the bank. Profit remittance to non-resident partners faces no legal hurdle once statutory accounts, partner resolutions, and tax declarations are in order.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline for the surrender of export proceeds and no mandatory conversion ratio in Luxembourg or at EU level. Export receipts Shell may be held in the original currency, converted freely, or retained in an operational foreign-currency account. If balance-of-payments reporting is applicable under ECB statistical requirements, the reporting obligation is discharged by the resident bank on behalf of the client at monthly aggregate reporting cycles; no enterprise-level declaration is required for ordinary Apple App Store or Google Play payouts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High subject to strict constraints. An EU-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) passporting into Luxembourg or a Luxembourg-licensed EMI may open multi-currency accounts fully remotely and can process large Apple App Store and Google Play settlement flows, provided the EMI obtains CSSF-authorised custody and safeguarding. However, a non-EEA offshore digital EMI is generally not viable as a primary treasury bank because it cannot legally provide safeguarded client-money accounts in Luxembourg, conduct FX forwards, or issue irrevocable payment guarantees. Such offshore EMIs should be considered only as auxiliary collection wallets, never as the sole clearing and treasury repository.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned SCSp, the general partner and each ultimately beneficial owner holding 25% or more must attend an in-person or video-recorded interview at a physical Luxembourg branch or via an approved CSSF-compliant video-identification process. Most tier-1 banks still require physical presence of the authorised representative for the initial account opening, notarisation of powers of attorney, and apostilled corporate documents for non-EU beneficial owners. Remote onboarding is legally possible under CSSF guidance using eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures and secure video transmission, but it is granted only at the bank's discretion; a physical onboarding cadence should be assumed as the baseline for scheduling liquidity infrastructure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is a partnership without separate legal personality; banks frequently flag ambiguity over who owns, binds, and controls the account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement and executed amended and restated limited partnership agreement; Luxembourg legal opinion confirming validity of the SCSp under the Law of 12 July 2013; RCS/LBR registration excerpt; complete register of partners and an up-to-date beneficial ownership declaration; resolutions appointing the general partner and authorised signatories; certified passport copies and powers of attorney for each signatory

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high inflow of offshore investor capital into a pass-through partnership used for global gaming royalties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference or source-of-funds confirmation from each investor's regulated home institution; certified wealth and source-of-wealth letters; proof of economic substance showing active MMORPG publishing, game licence agreements, Apple App Store and Google Play developer agreements; audited or management accounts for the last two years; regulatory or licensing status confirmation for the gaming software

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large volume of digital in-app purchase receipts from multiple payment rails; perceived risk of fraud, chargebacks, or unintentional CTF exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal treasury and AML operating policy; segregation of revenue accounts with a licensed PSP/EMI; transaction-monitoring controls narrative; monthly settlement statements from Apple App Store and Google Play showing platform payer identities and net amounts; a rational commercial model for the ISIC 5820 activity; VAT and CIT return evidence showing the activity footprint; a certified SOC 1 or SOC 2 report of the treasury-vendor chain if available

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for capital contributions from partners is executed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wire with the reference purpose code 'Capital Contribution / Equity Injection' and the SCSp's fully legal name and RCS number. No BCL permit is required. The receiving bank must complete sanctions screening and CDD verification; for cross-border wires above EUR 10,000, payment reference and ultimate originator/beneficiary data must comply with the EU Wire Transfer Regulation (EU) 2015/847. The bank credit narrative should include the executed capital call, partner subscription agreement, and proof that no part of funds derives from unlawful or prohibited sources. Apple App Store and Google Play payout flows should be routed separately—as current-account remuneration—rather than mingled with capital injections, using a distinct purpose code such as 'Software Royalty Proceeds'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing includes SEPA Credit Transfer, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer, and SWIFT MT103 for global vendor payments to game developers, cloud service providers, and marketing agencies; commercial documentary letters of credit (MT700/MT710 flow) are used only where a physical goods or contractual performance guarantee is required, such as hardware procurement or co-publishing advances. For high-frequency MMORPG operational payments, treasury should use a central multi-currency cash pool at the Luxembourg relationship bank, with sub-ledger tracking per Apple App Store, Google Play, and direct distribution contracts. Outbound disbursements are subject to no Luxembourg FX restriction, but each payment must respect the EU sub-threshold for transparency (USD/EUR equivalent) and the bank's own transaction-monitoring rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Delivery FX forwards (up to 12 months) with CSSF-authorised credit institutions, executed under ISDA 2002 or local master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for USD/EUR and CNY/EUR where offshore settlement is economically necessary, subject to EMIR DMA/transaction reporting

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, JPY/USD and selected regional currencies) with authorised banks for tenor-matched treasury risk management, provided that collateral and margin obligations comply with EMIR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year between 1 January and 31 March for data current as of 31 December of the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine from EUR 1,250 to EUR 125,000 for late or incomplete confirmation; deliberate false statements may trigger criminal sanctions and statutory liability of the general partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If filing is legally applicable, within seven months after the financial year-end (for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered coercive fines up to EUR 1,000 per day, personal liability of the general partner, and potential deregistration risk after repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax declaration for the tax-transparent SCSp and partner reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for the preceding calendar year; extended deadlines apply when filing electronically and on express request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and coercive penalties of up to EUR 2,500 per month, plus criminal sanctions for intentional non-declaration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The SCSp is not automatically subject to a Luxembourg statutory audit. A Luxembourg-approved independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is required if the entity is a regulated investment vehicle (SIF, SICAR, RAIF), a public-interest undertaking, or exceeds two of the following thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce of 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the modified law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts and the law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must confirm the RBE data through the Luxembourg Business Registers electronic portal each year before 31 March. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in control must be filed with the RBE within one month of the transaction, independently of the annual confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,000 – 6,500 per year for a Luxembourg registered office and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 – 30,000 per year for a Luxembourg statutory audit if the audit threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate statutory rate (17% national CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on the national CIT + average municipal business tax of 6.75% in Luxembourg City; the combined rate varies within a municipal range such as 20.97% to 26.84%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No universal tax holiday exists. Preferential tax instruments: (i) Luxembourg IP Box – 80% exemption of qualifying IP income, yielding an effective aggregate rate of approximately 5.05% for eligible game software copyrights; (ii) investment tax credit of up to 12% for eligible digital and technological investments; (iii) notional interest deduction (NID) on qualifying additional equity capital (annual rate, e.g. 4.10% for 2023). SCSp as a fiscally transparent partnership is not itself taxed; these incentives apply at partner level where the partner is a Luxembourg corporate taxpayer or PE.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 410 – Annual Partnership Return (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des sociétés de personnes), filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu / eCDF portal; where the SCSp is transparent this is essentially an income allocation return, indicating each partner’s share of taxable profit/loss. A Form 400 (Corporate Tax Return) is required only if the SCSp or partner-level permanent establishment is separately taxable, or in the case of an election to be taxed as a corporate entity.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end plus 5 months, i.e. 30 April for a calendar-year fiscal period; extended electronically to 31 May, and a reasoned extension to 31 July is routinely granted on application to the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp: name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, legal form code, business address, fiscal year start and end dates, and eCDF reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign general or limited partners must state their non-resident status and tax treaty residence; if the SCSp is treated as transparent, each partner’s personal tax identification number (TIN) should be listed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code and description, including ISIC 5820 / game publishing and the in-app purchase business model.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the exact income-generating activity (MMORPG publishing, in-app purchases, licensing of IP) to permit the tax authority to allocate permanent establishment and source income correctly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of accounting and valuation principles; balance sheet values; profit and loss position of the SCSp before partner allocation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that accounts are maintained under Luxembourg GAAP or IFRS and that the allocation percentages are contractually fixed; attach partnership agreement excerpts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable result and deductible items, including any qualifying IP-related deductions under the IP Box regime claimed at partner level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should not claim taxable losses of the SCSp unless they have a Luxembourg permanent establishment or the treaty in question assigns partnership income to the beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of intercompany transactions and transfer pricing documentation: controlled transactions with related parties by category, counterparty jurisdiction, and amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must confirm arm’s length remuneration for any services performed, IP royalties, or group funding through the SCSp; include Master File / Local File references.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information for the Luxembourg net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), to the extent the SCSp is subject to municipal business tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate if the SCSp is fiscally transparent for CIT and wealth tax; ensure the partner allocation schedule avoids double taxation with the foreign home jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fines up to EUR 5,000 per return; automatic late-payment interest of 0.55% per month (8.25% per annum) on any assessed tax due; if the return is deliberately false or fraudulent, evasion penalties range from 10% to 75% of the evaded tax, with imprisonment up to 5 years for fraudulent acts under Article 93 of the Luxembourg General Tax Code (AO).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends paid by a Luxembourg corporate entity. However, a SCSp is fiscally transparent: distributions from the SCSp to partners are generally not classified as dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at the partnership level. Where the SCSp engages in a commercial activity and maintains a Luxembourg permanent establishment, profits allocated to non-resident partners may be subject to municipal business tax but not to dividend WHT unless the partner is a Luxembourg tax-resident corporate shareholder under anti-abuse grounds.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA rates on Luxembourg-source income, if any withholding mechanism applies, the beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a valid Luxembourg Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) or, for foreign partners, a TRC from the DTA partner; (ii) submit Luxembourg Form 22 (or the electronic 'tarre a aplicar' relief application) before payment or within the statutory period; (iii) include a signed shareholder/beneficial ownership declaration; (iv) evidence full economic substance where the DTA contains a limitation-on-benefits (LOB) clause. For outbound dividend exemption, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive is implemented, subject to a 12-month holding period at 10% or more participation (except anti-abuse denial).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law generally imposes no withholding tax on outbound interest payments and no withholding tax on outbound royalty payments, except for payments to jurisdictions on certain harmful tax lists or in patent box abuse cases. Under many Luxembourg DTAs, reduced treaty rates for royalties range from 0% to 5% and for interest from 0% to 10%, but as Luxembourg does not typically levy source WHT, relief is ordinarily automatic. The EU Interest & Royalties Directive requires a 0% rate between associated companies resident in the EU, provided the beneficial owner is subject to tax and no anti-abuse circumvention exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) and Master File are mandatory when the group’s annual consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000 or equivalent in Luxembourg tax practice. For a lower-turnover SCSp group, the Luxembourg Local File / documentation obligation arises where controlled related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 for each transaction type, related-party trade balances exceed EUR 250,000, or aggregate controlled revenues exceed EUR 500,000 per fiscal year. In all cases, contemporaneous documentation demonstrating arm’s length compliance for any material intercompany transaction with related parties is required.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not operate Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations, but its administrative and anti-abuse doctrine requires genuine economic substance for treaty entitlement and CIT residency. The ‘substance doctrine’ applies through Article 6 of the Luxembourg General Tax Code and EU GAAR, requiring acts be lawful, non-abusive, and not solely directed at tax avoidance. For a SCSp engaged in hardcore MMORPG global publishing, indicators include: real offices, qualified staff making strategic game IP decisions, board/general partner meetings in Luxembourg, local bank accounts, comprehensive agreements, and functional management of in-app purchase revenue and platform payment rails. Absence of substance can trigger denial of tax residence, DTA relief denial, disallowance of IP deductions, and a 10% to 75% tax adjustment penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting a false Form 410/400, understating global in-app purchase revenue from Apple App Store or Google Play, omitting foreign PE income, or fabricating deductible expenses in the SCSp; deliberately manipulating partner allocations to avoid Luxembourg tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000 per false return; criminal fine of EUR 5,000 to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years under Article 93 AO; interest for late payment at 0.55% per month; in aggravated cases, tax uplift of up to 100%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may be jointly and severally liable for the tax debt where they ordered or caused the false declaration. In criminal proceedings, directors face personal criminal fines, confiscation orders, travel bans while proceedings are pending, and imprisonment; the general partner of an SCSp is personally liable for partnership debts, including tax assessments, without limit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Lack of Arm’s Length Evidence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging an intercompany royalty for MMORPG IP at a rate materially below market value, paying a cost-plus margin to the SCSp that does not reflect functional analysis, lacking contemporaneous local file, or structuring platform payouts to shift profits to a zero-tax related publisher outside the DTA network.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment by the Luxembourg tax authority to arm’s length standard, additional taxable income allocated to the SCSp or Luxembourg PE, penalties for failure to maintain documentation ranging from 10% to 50% of the adjusted profit, plus monthly late interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and compliance officer may be personally liable for restitution of the under-declared tax if they knowingly approved the inflated royalty or intercompany invoice trail; courts may impose bans on directorial positions and injunctions against leaving the jurisdiction pending tax audit completion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Tax Structured DTA Traps
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a shell without any real game-management activities, using the transparent partnership only to channel Apple/Google platform payouts to foreign partners with no substantive decision-making; relying on a DTA without a Luxembourg business purpose or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg authorities and foreign DTA partners may refuse treaty benefits; the tax authority will impose the 15% withholding tax on deemed distributions, disallow IP-box exemption, retroactively reassess profit with 100% top-up, and apply penalties up to 10% to 75% of the corrected tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners, and the SCSp general partner may face civil restitution for the resulting tax liability as de facto managers; personal criminal liability can include imprisonment up to 5 years for aggravated tax fraud committed through a sham structure; international tax cooperation can lead to asset freezes and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership / UBO Register Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an SCSp to conceal the real ultimate beneficial owners of the MMORPG revenue stream; failure to file the Luxembourg UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), failure to conduct AML due diligence on partners where the SCSp is subject to the law of 12 November 2004 (as amended), or making false statements in the beneficial ownership declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 to EUR 5,000,000 for legal entities and up to EUR 5,000,000 for responsible persons for AML violations; criminal sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years and criminal fines of up to EUR 150,000; the UBO filing omissions lead to additional penalties of up to EUR 1,000 per month or more; authorities may freeze funds and refuse tax clearances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and any director of a corporate general partner are personally liable for unjustified distributions, restitution orders, and AML penalties. Travel bans may be issued in the context of criminal asset recovery; imprisonment for personal involvement in laundering proceeds from unlawful in-app activities is available under the Luxembourg Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Payment Rails / Fiscal Transparency Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving app-platform payouts from Apple App Store and Google Play without recognizing Luxembourg-source taxable income, failing to include the payouts in the SCSp allocation schedule, or failing to file the annual Form 410 altogether while operating an unregistered Luxembourg permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate assessment based on estimated income; late filing fines; tax interest 0.55% per month; for a second offense, administrative fine doubles to EUR 10,000; refusal to comply may result in mandatory withholding tax collection from the SCSp’s bank accounts and injunction of payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot hide behind the SCSp corporate veil: the unlimited liability of the general partner applies to tax debts, and personal civil liability for unpaid taxes follows if the directors acted in bad faith or with gross negligence. Criminal exposure for willful non-payment can carry imprisonment up to 5 years and a travel ban during criminal investigation.
